research_question: How do rotation periods of magnetic chemically peculiar (mCP) stars derived from TESS data compare with previously published literature periods, specifically those from the International Variable Star Index (VSX)?

phase_1.user_prompt: I am characterizing the photometric variability of a sample of magnetic chemically peculiar (mCP) stars originally discovered in LAMOST DR4. To compare my newly derived TESS rotation periods against existing literature, I need to retrieve known variable star periods and variability types. Which primary VizieR catalog designation corresponds to the AAVSO International Variable Star Index (VSX), the most comprehensive and up-to-date collection of variable star data?

phase_2.user_prompt: Now that we've identified the AAVSO International Variable Star Index as our reference, query the VizieR catalog B/vsx to retrieve the literature variability type and period for one of our mCP stars located at RA 00h08m40.998s, Dec +58d02m13.20s (J2000). Use a small search radius of 3 arcseconds to avoid mismatched background sources.
